articles.headline: Festival Stampede in Kolkata Kills at Least 17
articles.brief: A tragic crowd crush during a festival in Kolkata, India, has left at least 17 people dead. Local media reports and officials suggest that poor crowd control exacerbated by sudden rain led to the deadly stampede.

articles.headline: Egypt Ready to Support Saudi Arabia Against Houthi Threats
articles.brief: Cairo has formally announced its readiness to provide Saudi Arabia with all necessary military and strategic support amidst ongoing escalations involving Houthi conflicts in the region.

articles.headline: Lithuania Attributes Starlink Arson Attack to Russian Sabotage
articles.brief: Lithuanian authorities have officially stated that an attempted arson attack targeting Starlink infrastructure was a coordinated act of sabotage linked directly to Russian operatives.

articles.headline: China Proposes Export Controls on Solar Manufacturing Tech
articles.brief: Beijing has proposed comprehensive export controls on advanced solar-manufacturing technologies, a move that could significantly reshape global supply chains for renewable energy equipment.

articles.headline: US Treasury Chief Criticizes Europe Over Russian Oil Tariffs
articles.brief: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized European allies for refusing Washington's request to impose secondary tariffs on India and China for purchasing Russian oil, questioning the burden distribution.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Rules Internet Access a Fundamental Right for Children
articles.brief: India's Supreme Court has declared that children possess a fundamental right to access and use the internet, criticizing blanket bans as disproportionate measures and favoring parental oversight instead.

articles.headline: Central Bank of India Reports 21% Q2 Net Profit Surge
articles.brief: The Central Bank of India announced a 21% increase in its second-quarter net profit, reaching ₹1,469 crore, driven significantly by higher core income and expanded operational revenues.

articles.headline: Microsoft Pulls Out of UK Data Center Deal with Nscale
articles.brief: Tech giant Microsoft has reportedly withdrawn from a high-profile UK data center partnership with Nscale, according to recent media reports from the Telegraph.

articles.headline: Samsung to Use TSMC Tech for Nvidia's Next-Gen Memory
articles.brief: Reports indicate that Samsung plans to utilize TSMC's advanced manufacturing technology to produce Nvidia's next-generation memory chips, according to industry sources in Seoul.

articles.headline: Milan Police Clash with Protesters Over Cost of Living
articles.brief: Violent clashes broke out between Milan police and demonstrators protesting soaring living costs and declining public services, marking a second consecutive day of civil unrest in Italy.

articles.headline: India's Crude Import Bill Surges 46% Amid Soaring Prices
articles.brief: India's crude oil import bill surged by 46% in September as global energy prices climbed sharply, putting additional pressure on the nation's trade deficit and foreign exchange reserves.

articles.headline: Ukraine Successfully Strikes Saint Petersburg Oil Refinery
articles.brief: Ukrainian forces launched a successful drone strike targeting an oil refinery located in Saint Petersburg, causing significant structural damage and escalating energy infrastructure warfare.

articles.headline: NCB Busts Synthetic Drug Labs in Greater Noida, Arrests Two
articles.brief: The Narcotics Control Bureau successfully busted two illicit synthetic drug manufacturing laboratories in Greater Noida, arresting two individuals including a foreign national.

articles.headline: Trump Endorses Netanyahu in Close Israeli Election
articles.brief: Former US President Donald Trump has officially endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu as the tight race in the Israeli general election approaches its decisive final stages.

articles.headline: IMF and World Bank Meetings Leave Developing Nations Concerned
articles.brief: The latest joint meetings of the IMF and World Bank concluded without definitive resolutions, leaving developing nations grappling with heavy debt burdens and unanswered economic questions.
